sa: जानश्रुतिर् ह पौत्रायणः श्रद्धादेयो बहुदायी बहुपाक्य आस ।
स ह सर्वत आवसथान् मापयां चक्रे सर्वत एव मे ऽन्नम् अत्स्यन्तीति ॥
iast: jānaśrutir ha pautrāyaṇaḥ śraddhādeyo bahudāyī bahupākya āsa ।
sa ha sarvata āvasathān māpayāṃ cakre sarvata eva me ’nnam atsyantīti ॥
words: to cause to be measured or built

tr.text: Om. There lived Janasruti Pautrayana who made gifts with respect, who gave liberally, and who had much food cooked (for others). He built rest-houses all round, thinking, ‘Everywhere people will eat of my food’.

sa: हो हो ऽयि भल्लाक्ष भल्लाक्ष जानश्रुतेः पौत्रायणस्य समं दिवा ज्योतिर् आततं तन् मा प्रसाङ्क्षीस् तत् त्वां मा प्रधाक्षीर् इति ॥
iast: ho ho ’yi bhallākṣa bhallākṣa jānaśruteḥ pautrāyaṇasya samaṃ divā jyotir ātataṃ tan mā prasāṅkṣīs tat tvāṃ mā pradhākṣīr iti ॥
words: to address or salute with reverence
a vocative particle (especially used in dramas)
a term used in addressing a flamingo
a term used in addressing a flamingo

tr.text: Once at night, the swans flew along. Then one swan addressed another swan thus, ‘Ho, Ho, O Bhallaksa, Bhallaksa, the effulgence of Janasruti Pautrayana has spread like the heaven. Do not come in touch with it, lest it should scorch you.’

sa: तम् उ ह परः प्रत्युवाच कम् व् अर एनम् एतत् सन्तं सयुग्वानम् इव रैक्वम् आत्थ इति ।
यो नु कथं सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ॥
iast: tam u ha paraḥ pratyuvāca kam v ara enam etat santaṃ sayugvānam iva raikvam āttha iti ।
yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti ॥

tr.text: Bhallaksa replied to him, ‘lo, how could you so describe him as if he were Raikva with the cart ?’ ‘Of what sort is this Raikva with the cart ?’

sa: यथा कृताय विजितायाधरेयाः संयन्त्य् एवम् एनं सर्वं तद् अभिसमेति यत् किंच प्रजाः साधु कुर्वन्ति ।
यस् तद् वेद यत् स वेद स मयैतद् उक्त इति ॥
iast: yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃca prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti ।
yas tad veda yat sa veda sa mayaitad ukta iti ॥
words: away with; enough of; no need of

tr.text: ‘Just as all the lower casts of the dice go over to one who has won the Krita-cast, so does go over to Raikva whatsoever good the creatures do; so also to him who knows what Raikva knows. Such is he who has thus been spoken of by me.’

sa: तद् उ ह जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायण उपशुश्राव ।
स ह संजिहान एव क्षत्तारम् उवाचाङ्गारे ह सयुग्वानम् इव रैक्वम् आत्थेति ।
यो नु कथं सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ॥
iast: tad u ha jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇa upaśuśrāva ।
sa ha saṃjihāna eva kṣattāram uvācāṅgāre ha sayugvānam iva raikvam āttheti ।
yo nu kathaṃ sayugvā raikva iti ॥
words: one who cuts or carves or distributes anything

tr.text: Janasruti Pautrayana overheard those words. As soon as he arose, he said to the attendant, ‘Lo, did you praise me like Raikva with the cart ?’ ‘What sort of man is this Raikva with the cart ?’ (Janasruti repeated the words of the swan): ‘Just as all the lower casts of the dice go over to one who has won the Krita-cast, so does go over to Raikva whatsoever good the creatures do; and so also to him who knows what Raikva knows. Such is he who has thus been spoken of by me’.

sa: यथा कृताय विजितायाधरेयाः संयन्त्य् एवम् एनं सर्वं तद् अभिसमेति यत् किंच प्रजाः साधु कुर्वन्ति ।
यस् तद् वेद यत् स वेद स मयैतद् उक्त इति ॥
iast: yathā kṛtāya vijitāyādhareyāḥ saṃyanty evam enaṃ sarvaṃ tad abhisameti yat kiṃca prajāḥ sādhu kurvanti ।
yas tad veda yat sa veda sa mayaitad ukta iti ॥
words: away with; enough of; no need of

tr.text: Janasruti Pautrayana overheard those words. As soon as he arose, he said to the attendant, ‘Lo, did you praise me like Raikva with the cart ?’ ‘What sort of man is this Raikva with the cart ?’ (Janasruti repeated the words of the swan): ‘Just as all the lower casts of the dice go over to one who has won the Krita-cast, so does go over to Raikva whatsoever good the creatures do; and so also to him who knows what Raikva knows. Such is he who has thus been spoken of by me’.

sa: स ह क्षत्तान्विष्य नाविदम् इति प्रत्येयाय ।
तं होवाच यत्रारे ब्राह्मणस्यान्वेषणा तद् एनम् अर्च्छेति ॥
iast: sa ha kṣattānviṣya nāvidam iti pratyeyāya ।
taṃ hovāca yatrāre brāhmaṇasyānveṣaṇā tad enam arccheti ॥
words: one who cuts or carves or distributes anything

tr.text: The attendant, having searched for him, came back thinking, ‘I could not find him’. Janasruti said to him, ‘Well, where the knower of Brahman should be searched for there search for him’.

sa: सो ऽधस्ताच् छकटस्य पामानं कषमाणम् उपोपविवेश ।
तं हाभ्युवाद त्वं नु भगवः सयुग्वा रैक्व इति ।
अहं ह्य् अरा ३ इति ह प्रतिजज्ञे ।
iast: taṃ hābhyuvāda tvaṃ nu bhagavaḥ sayugvā raikva iti ।
ahaṃ hy arā 3 iti ha pratijajñe ।
words: to sit down or take a seat by the side of
to address or salute with reverence
one who cuts or carves or distributes anything

tr.text: (After searching) he came to a man sitting under a cart and scratching eruptions on his skin and, sitting near him, asked him, ‘Revered sir, are you Raikva with the cart ?’ ‘Well fellow, yes, I am’, he admitted. Thinking ‘I have found him’, the attendant returned.

sa: तद् उ ह जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणः षट् शतानि गवां निष्कम् अश्वतरीरथं तद् आदाय प्रतिचक्रमे ।
iast: tad u ha jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ ṣaṭ śatāni gavāṃ niṣkam aśvatarīrathaṃ tad ādāya praticakrame ।
words: a golden ornament for the neck or breast

tr.text: On hearing this, Janasruti Pautrayana took with him six hundred cows, a gold necklace, and a chariot drawn by mules and went to Raikva and addressed him thus: ‘O Raikva, (here are for you) these six hundred cows, this gold necklace, and this chariot drawn by mules. Now, revered sir, instruct me about the deity whom you worship.’

sa: रैक्वेमानि षट् शतानि गवाम् अयं निष्को ऽयम् अश्वतरीरथः ।
अनु म एतां भगवो देवतां शाधि यां देवताम् उपास्स इति ॥
iast: raikvemāni ṣaṭ śatāni gavām ayaṃ niṣko ’yam aśvatarīrathaḥ ।
anu ma etāṃ bhagavo devatāṃ śādhi yāṃ devatām upāssa iti ॥
words: a golden ornament for the neck or breast

tr.text: On hearing this, Janasruti Pautrayana took with him six hundred cows, a gold necklace, and a chariot drawn by mules and went to Raikva and addressed him thus: ‘O Raikva, (here are for you) these six hundred cows, this gold necklace, and this chariot drawn by mules. Now, revered sir, instruct me about the deity whom you worship.’

sa: तम् उ ह परः प्रत्युवाचाह हारेत्वा शूद्र तवैव सह गोभिर् अस्त्व् इति ।
तद् उ ह पुनर् एव जानश्रुतिः पौत्रायणः सहस्रं गवां निष्कम् अश्वतरीरथं दुहितरं तद् आदाय प्रतिचक्रमे ॥
iast: tam u ha paraḥ pratyuvācāha hāretvā śūdra tavaiva saha gobhir astv iti ।
tad u ha punar eva jānaśrutiḥ pautrāyaṇaḥ sahasraṃ gavāṃ niṣkam aśvatarīrathaṃ duhitaraṃ tad ādāya praticakrame ॥
words: a golden ornament for the neck or breast
a daughter (the milker or drawing milk from her mother)

tr.text: The other man answered him thus: ‘Ah, O Sudra, let this gold necklace together with the chariot and the cows remain with you.’ Thereupon Janasruti Pautrayana again took with him one thousand cows, a gold necklace, a chariot drawn by mules and his daughter and went over to Raikva.

sa: रैक्वेदं सहस्रं गवाम् अयं निष्को ऽयम् अश्वतरीरथ इयं जायायं ग्रामो यस्मिन्न् आस्से ऽन्व् एव मा भगवः शाधीति ॥
iast: raikvedaṃ sahasraṃ gavām ayaṃ niṣko ’yam aśvatarīratha iyaṃ jāyāyaṃ grāmo yasminn āsse ’nv eva mā bhagavaḥ śādhīti ॥
words: a golden ornament for the neck or breast

tr.text: Janasruti said to him: ‘O Raikva, (here are for you) these one thousand cows, this gold necklace, this chariot drawn by mules, this wife, and this village in which you reside. Now, revered sir, please instruct me’.

sa: तस्या ह मुखम् उपोद्गृह्णन्न् उवाचाजहारेमाः शूद्रानेनैव मुखेनालापयिष्यथा इति ।
ते हैते रैक्वपर्णा नाम महावृषेषु यत्रास्मा उवास ।
iast: tasyā ha mukham upodgṛhṇann uvācājahāremāḥ śūdrānenaiva mukhenālāpayiṣyathā iti ।
te haite raikvaparṇā nāma mahāvṛṣeṣu yatrāsmā uvāsa ।
words: to bring near (to the mouth) after (others have done so)

tr.text: Taking that princess to be the portal for the conveying of knowledge, Raikva said, ‘O Sudra, you have brought all these ! Even by this means (i.e. the princess) you will make me talk.’ The king gave away to him all those villages in the Mahavrisa country known as Raikvaparna where Raikva lived. Raikva said to him:

sa: यदा वा अग्निर् उद्वायति वायुम् एवाप्येति ।
यदा सूर्यो ऽस्तम् एति वायुम् एवाप्येति ।
यदा चन्द्रो ऽस्तम् एति वायुम् एवाप्येति ॥
iast: yadā vā agnir udvāyati vāyum evāpyeti ।
words: setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)
setting (as of the sun or of luminaries)

tr.text: Air indeed is the absorber. For when a fire goes out, it is in air that it merges; when the sun sets, it is in air that it merges; when the moon sets, it is in air that it merges.
When water dries up, it is in air that it merges; for air absorbs all these. This is (the doctrine of Samvarga) with reference to the gods.

sa: स यदा स्वपिति प्राणम् एव वाग् अप्य् एति ।
प्राणो ह्य् एवैतान् सर्वान् संवृङ्क्त इति ॥
iast: sa yadā svapiti prāṇam eva vāg apy eti ।
prāṇo hy evaitān sarvān saṃvṛṅkta iti ॥

tr.text: Next is (the doctrine of Samvarga) with reference to the body: Prana indeed is the absorber. When one sleeps, speech merges in Prana, the eye merges in Prana, the ear merges in Prana, the mind merges in Prana: for Prana, indeed, absorbs all these.
These, indeed, are the two absorbers: Air among the gods and Prana among the sense-organs.

sa: अथ ह शौनकं च कापेयम् अभिप्रतारिणं च काक्षसेनिं परिविष्यमाणौ ब्रह्मचारी बिभिक्षे ।
iast: atha ha śaunakaṃ ca kāpeyam abhipratāriṇaṃ ca kākṣaseniṃ pariviṣyamāṇau brahmacārī bibhikṣe ।
words: name of various authors and teachers
name of a descendant of Kakṣasena
a young Brāhman before marriage (in the first period of his life)

tr.text: Once upon a time, while Kapeya Saunaka and Kaksaseni Abhipratarin were being served with food, a celibate student of sacred knowledge begged of them. They did not give him anything.

sa: महात्मनश् चतुरो देव एकः कः स जगार भुवनस्य गोपाः ।
तं कापेय नाभिपश्यन्ति मर्त्या अभिप्रतारिन् बहुधा वसन्तम् ।
यस्मै वा एतद् अन्नं तस्मा एतन् न दत्तम् इति ॥
iast: mahātmanaś caturo deva ekaḥ kaḥ sa jagāra bhuvanasya gopāḥ ।
taṃ kāpeya nābhipaśyanti martyā abhipratārin bahudhā vasantam ।
yasmai vā etad annaṃ tasmā etan na dattam iti ॥
words: name of a descendant of Kakṣasena
in many ways or parts or forms or directions

tr.text: The Brahmacharin said, ‘Prajapati, the one god swallowed up the four great ones; he is the protector of the worlds. O Kapeya, O Abhipratarin, mortals do not see him who dwells variously. Even from him, for whom all this food is meant, you have withheld it.’

sa: तद् उ ह शौनकः कापेयः प्रतिमन्वानः प्रत्येयाय ।
आत्मा देवानां जनिता प्रजानां हिरङ्यदंष्ट्रो बभसो ऽनसूरिः ।
महान्तम् अस्य महिमानम् आहुर् अनद्यमानो यद् अनन्नम् अत्ति ।
इति वै वयम् ब्रह्मचारिन् नेदम् उपास्महे दत्तास्मै भिक्षाम् इति ॥
iast: tad u ha śaunakaḥ kāpeyaḥ pratimanvānaḥ pratyeyāya ।
ātmā devānāṃ janitā prajānāṃ hiraṅyadaṃṣṭro babhaso ’nasūriḥ ।
mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur anadyamāno yad anannam atti ।
iti vai vayam brahmacārin nedam upāsmahe dattāsmai bhikṣām iti ॥
words: name of various authors and teachers
to render back in return or in reply
rice or food undeserving of its name
a young Brāhman before marriage (in the first period of his life)
the act of begging or asking

tr.text: Kapeya Saunaka, reflecting on those words, approached him (and said): ‘He who is the self of all gods and the creator of all beings, who has undecaying teeth, who is the devourer, who is the wise one, who is himself never eaten (but) who devours even those who are not food; and hence (the knowers) describe his magnificence as immeasurable – such, indeed, is the Brahman, O Brahmacharin, whom we worship’. (Then he told the servants): ‘Give him food’.

sa: ते वा एते पञ्चान्ये पञ्चान्ये दश सन्तस् तत् कृतम् ।
तस्मात् सर्वासु दिक्ष्व् अन्नम् एव दश कृतम् ।
सर्वम् अस्य इदं दृष्टं भवत्य् अन्नादो भवति य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ॥
iast: te vā ete pañcānye pañcānye daśa santas tat kṛtam ।
tasmāt sarvāsu dikṣv annam eva daśa kṛtam ।
sarvam asya idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavaty annādo bhavati ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: They gave him food. Now, these five and the other five, together becoming ten, constitute the Krita (dice-cast). Therefore (i.e. because the number ten applies to both), these ten are the food or Virat dwelling in all the ten quarters, and these are (the enjoyer) Krita. This Virat, of the form of ten deities, again, is the eater of food (as Krita); by him all this is perceived. He who sees thus, by him also all this is perceived, and he becomes as eater of food.

sa: सत्यकामो ह जाबालो जबालां मातरम् आमन्त्रयां चक्रे ।
ब्रह्मचर्यं भवति विवत्स्यामि किंगोत्रो न्व् अहम् अस्मीति ॥
iast: satyakāmo ha jābālo jabālāṃ mātaram āmantrayāṃ cakre ।
brahmacaryaṃ bhavati vivatsyāmi kiṃgotro nv aham asmīti ॥

tr.text: Once upon a time Satyakama Jabala addressed his mother Jabala, ‘Mother, I desire to live the life of a celibate student of sacred knowledge in the teacher’s house. Of what lineage am I ?’

sa: नाहम् एतद् वेद तात यद्गोत्रस् त्वम् असि ।
बह्व् अहम् चरन्ती परिचारिणी यौवने त्वाम् अलभे ।
साहम् एतन् न वेद यद्गोत्रस् त्वम् असि ।
स सत्यकाम एव जाबालो ब्रुवीथा इति ॥
iast: nāham etad veda tāta yadgotras tvam asi ।
bahv aham carantī paricāriṇī yauvane tvām alabhe ।
sāham etan na veda yadgotras tvam asi ।
sa satyakāma eva jābālo bruvīthā iti ॥

tr.text: She said to him, ‘My child, I do not know of what lineage you are. I, who was engaged in many works and in attending on others, got you in my youth. Having been such I could not know of what lineage you are. However, I am Jabala by name and you are named Satyakama. So you speak of yourself only as Satyakama Jabala.’
He went to Haridrumata Gautama and said, ‘I desire to live under you, revered sir, as a Brahmacharin; may I approach your venerable self (for the same) ?’

sa: नाहम् एतद् वेद भो यद्गोत्रो ऽहम् अस्मि ।
सा मा प्रत्यब्रवीद् बह्व् अहम् चरन्ती परिचरिणी यौवने त्वाम् अलभे ।
साहम् एतन् न वेद यद्गोत्रस् त्वम् असि ।
सो ऽहं सत्यकामो जाबालो ऽस्मि भो इति ॥
iast: nāham etad veda bho yadgotro ’ham asmi ।
sā mā pratyabravīd bahv aham carantī paricariṇī yauvane tvām alabhe ।
sāham etan na veda yadgotras tvam asi ।

tr.text: Gautama asked him, ‘Dear boy, of what lineage are you ?’ He replied, ‘Sir, I do not know of what lineage I am. I asked my mother; she replied, "I, who was engaged in many works and in attending on others, got you in my youth. Having been such, I could not know of what lineage you are. However, I am Jabala by name and you are named Satyakama". So, sir, I am Satyakama Jabala.’

sa: उप त्वा नेष्ये न सत्याद् अगा इति ।
तम् उपनीय कृशानाम् अबलानां चतुःशता गा निराकृत्य उवाचेमाः सोम्यानुसंव्रजेति ।
iast: upa tvā neṣye na satyād agā iti ।
tam upanīya kṛśānām abalānāṃ catuḥśatā gā nirākṛtya uvācemāḥ somyānusaṃvrajeti ।
words: to drive (as the cattle to pasture)

tr.text: The teacher said to him, ‘No one who is not a Brahmana can speak thus. Dear boy, bring the sacrificial fuel, I shall initiate you as a Brahmacharin, for you have not deviated from truth’. Having initiated him, he sorted out four hundred lean and weak cows and said, ‘Dear boy, follow them.’ While he was driving them towards the forest Satyakama said, ‘I shall not return till it is one thousand.’ He lived away for a long time, till they had increased to one thousand.

sa: अथ हैनम् ऋषभो ऽभ्युवाद सत्यकाम ३ इति ।
words: to address or salute with reverence

tr.text: Then the bull addressed him thus, ‘Satyakama !’ ‘Yes, revered sir’, thus he responded, ‘Dear boy, we have reached a thousand, take us to the house of the teacher.’

sa: ब्रह्मणश् च ते पादं ब्रवाणि इति ।
एष वै सोम्य चतुष्कलः पादो ब्रह्मणः प्रकाशवान् नाम ॥
iast: brahmaṇaś ca te pādaṃ bravāṇi iti ।
eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān nāma ॥
words: having 4 marks (on the thumb denoting the proficiency in the 4 Vedas)

tr.text: ‘Let me instruct you about one foot of Brahman also’. ‘Please instruct me, revered sir.’ (The bull) said to him, ‘The eastern quarter is one part, the western quarter is one part, the southern quarter is one part, the northern quarter is one part. This indeed, dear boy, is one foot of Brahman, consisting of four, named the Radiant.

sa: स य एतम् एवं विद्वांश् चतुष्कलं पादं ब्रह्मणः प्रकाशवान् इत्य् उपास्ते प्रकाशवान् अस्मिंल् लोके भवति ।
प्रकाशवतो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतम् एवं विद्वांश् चतुष्कलं पादं ब्रह्मणः प्रकाशवान् इत्य् उपास्ते ॥
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān ity upāste prakāśavān asmiṃl loke bhavati ।
prakāśavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇaḥ prakāśavān ity upāste ॥

having 4 marks (on the thumb denoting the proficiency in the 4 Vedas)

tr.text: ‘He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Radiant, becomes radiant in this world. He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Radiant, wins the radiant regions (in the next world).’

sa: स ह श्वो भूते गा अभिप्रस्थापयां चकार ।
ता यत्राभिसायं बभूवुस् तत्राग्निम् उपसमाधाय गा उपरुध्य समिधम् आधाय पश्चाद् अग्नेः प्राङ् उपोपविवेश ॥
iast: sa ha śvo bhūte gā abhiprasthāpayāṃ cakāra ।
tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvus tatrāgnim upasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidham ādhāya paścād agneḥ prāṅ upopaviveśa ॥

tr.text: ‘Fire will tell you of one foot of Brahman’. At dawn of the next day he drove the cows towards the teacher’s house. Towards evening, at the place where those cows came together, he kindled the fire there, penned the cows, laid on fuel and sat down near them behind the fire, facing the east.

words: to address or salute with reverence

tr.text: The fire addressed him, ‘Satyakama !’ ‘Yes, revered sir’, he responded.

sa: एष वै सोम्य चतुष्कलः पादो ब्रह्मणो ऽनन्तवान् नाम ॥
iast: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇo ’nantavān nāma ॥

This indeed, dear boy, is one foot of Brahman, consisting of four parts, named the Endless.

tr.text: ‘He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Endless, becomes endless in this world. He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Endless, wins the endless (undecaying) regions.’

sa: हꣳसस्ते पादं वक्तेति स ह श्वोभूते गा
iast: haꣳsaste pādaṃ vakteti sa ha śvobhūte gā
words: what may happen morrow; next day

Towards evening, at the place where the cows came together, he kindled the fire there, penned the cows, laid on fuel and sat down near them behind the fire facing the east.
The swan flew to him and addressed him, ‘Satyakama !’ ‘Yes, revered sir’, he responded.

This indeed, dear boy, is one foot of Brahman, consisting of four parts, named the Effulgent.

ज्योतिष्मतो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतम् एवं विद्वांश् चतुष्कलं पादं ब्रह्मणो ज्योतिष्मान् इत्य् उपास्ते ॥

He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Effulgent, wins the effulgent regions (of the sun, the moon, etc., in the next world).’

ता यत्राभिसायं बभूवुस् तत्राग्निम् उपसमाधाय गा उपरुध्य समिधम् आधाय पश्चाद् अग्नेः प्राङ् उपोपविवेश ॥

tā yatrābhisāyaṃ babhūvus tatrāgnim upasamādhāya gā uparudhya samidham ādhāya paścād agneḥ prāṅ upopaviveśa ॥

tr.text: ‘Madgu will tell you of one foot of Brahman’. At dawn of the next day, he drove the cows towards the teacher’s house. Towards evening at the place where the cows came together, he kindled the fire there, penned the cows, laid on fuel and sat down near them behind the fire facing the east.

words: a diver-bird (a kind of aquatic bird or cormorant)
to address or salute with reverence

tr.text: The Madgu bird flew to him and addressed him, ‘Satyakama !’ ‘Yes, revered sir’, he responded.

sa: एष वै सोम्य चतुष्कलः पादो ब्रह्मण आयतनवान् नाम ॥
iast: eṣa vai somya catuṣkalaḥ pādo brahmaṇa āyatanavān nāma ॥
words: having 4 marks (on the thumb denoting the proficiency in the 4 Vedas)
name of the fourth foot of Brahman

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, let me instruct you about one foot of Brahman’. ‘Please instruct me, revered sir’. (The Madgu bird) said to him, ‘Prana is one part, the eye is one part, the ear is one part, and the mind is one part. This indeed, dear boy, is one foot of Brahman, consisting of four parts, named the Repository.

sa: स य एतम् एवं विद्वांश् चतुष्कलं पादं ब्रह्मण आयतनवान् इत्य् उपास्त आयतनवान् अस्मिंल् लोके भवति ।
आयतनवतो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतम् एवं विद्वांश् चतुष्कलं पादं ब्रह्मण आयतनवान् इत्य् उपास्ते ॥
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇa āyatanavān ity upāsta āyatanavān asmiṃl loke bhavati ।
āyatanavato ha lokāñ jayati ya etam evaṃ vidvāṃś catuṣkalaṃ pādaṃ brahmaṇa āyatanavān ity upāste ॥
words: having 4 marks (on the thumb denoting the proficiency in the 4 Vedas)
name of the fourth foot of Brahman
having 4 marks (on the thumb denoting the proficiency in the 4 Vedas)
name of the fourth foot of Brahman

tr.text: ‘He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Repository, becomes repository (i.e. with proper abode) in this world. He who knows this one foot of Brahman consisting of four parts thus, and meditates on it as the Repository, wins the repository (i.e. extensive) regions (in the next world).’

words: to address or salute with reverence

tr.text: Satyakama reached the house of the teacher. The teacher addressed him, ‘Satyakama !’ ‘Yes, revered sir’, he responded.

sa: भगवांस् त्व् एव मे कामे ब्रूयात् ॥
iast: bhagavāṃs tv eva me kāme brūyāt ॥

tr.text: ‘Dear boy, you shine like a knower of Brahman; who is it that has instructed you ?’ Satyakama assured him, ‘People other than men. But I wish, revered sir, that you would expound it to me.

sa: श्रुतं ह्य् एव मे भगवद्दृशेभ्य आचार्याद् धैव विद्या विदिता साधिष्ठं प्रापतीति ।
अत्र ह न किंचन वीयायेति वीयायेति ॥
iast: śrutaṃ hy eva me bhagavaddṛśebhya ācāryād dhaiva vidyā viditā sādhiṣṭhaṃ prāpatīti ।
atra ha na kiṃcana vīyāyeti vīyāyeti ॥

tr.text: ‘I have definitely heard from persons like your venerable self that the knowledge directly learnt from one’s own teacher becomes most beneficial’. The teacher taught him the same thing, and nothing was omitted from this – yea, nothing was omitted.

sa: उपकोसलो ह वै कामलायनः सत्यकामे जाबाले ब्रह्मचार्यम् उवास ।
तस्य ह द्वादश वार्षान्य् अग्नीन् परिचचार ।
स ह स्मान्यान् अन्तेवासिनः समावर्तयंस् तं ह स्मैव न समावर्तयति ॥
iast: upakosalo ha vai kāmalāyanaḥ satyakāme jābāle brahmacāryam uvāsa ।
tasya ha dvādaśa vārṣāny agnīn paricacāra ।
sa ha smānyān antevāsinaḥ samāvartayaṃs taṃ ha smaiva na samāvartayati ॥
words: a pupil who dwells near or in the house of his teacher

tr.text: Once upon a time Upakosala Kamalayana lived with Satyakama Jabala the life of a Brahmacharin. He tended his fires for twelve years. Satyakama performed for other disciples the ceremony of completing studies and returning home, but did not perform the ceremony for Upakosala.

sa: तं जायोवाच तप्तो ब्रह्मचारी कुशलम् अग्नीन् परिचचारीत् ।
iast: taṃ jāyovāca tapto brahmacārī kuśalam agnīn paricacārīt ।
words: a young Brāhman before marriage (in the first period of his life)
to tell anything earlier than another person (acc.)

tr.text: The wife of the teacher said to him, ‘This Brahmacharin has undergone severe austerities and has tended the fires properly; you should teach him so that the fires may not blame you.’ But the teacher went away on a journey without instructing him.

sa: स ह उवाच बहव इमे ऽस्मिन् पुरुषे कामा नानात्यायाः ।
iast: sa ha uvāca bahava ime ’smin puruṣe kāmā nānātyāyāḥ ।
words: a young Brāhman before marriage (in the first period of his life)

tr.text: Through mental sufferings Upakosala began to fast. The wife of the teacher said to him, ‘O Brahmacharin, do eat; why are you not eating ?’ He replied, ‘In this (very ordinary and disappointed) man (i.e. myself) there are many desires running in various directions; I am full of mental sufferings; so I shall not eat.’

sa: प्राणो ब्रह्म कं ब्रह्म खं ब्रह्मेति ॥
iast: prāṇo brahma kaṃ brahma khaṃ brahmeti ॥
words: a young Brāhman before marriage (in the first period of his life)
an exclamation or inceptive particle (expressive of an exhortation to do anythin

tr.text: Thereupon the fires said among themselves, ‘This Brahmacharin has undergone severe austerities and has tended us properly; come let us instruct him’. They then said to him, ‘Prana (life) is Brahman, Ka (joy) is Brahman, Kha (ether) is Brahman’.

sa: कं च तु खं च न विजानामीति ।
यद् वाव कं तद् एव खम् ।
यद् एव खं तद् एव कम् इति ।
प्राणं च हास्मै तद् आकाशं चोचुः ॥
iast: kaṃ ca tu khaṃ ca na vijānāmīti ।
yad vāva kaṃ tad eva kham ।
yad eva khaṃ tad eva kam iti ।
prāṇaṃ ca hāsmai tad ākāśaṃ cocuḥ ॥

tr.text: He said, ‘I understand that Prana is Brahman; but I do not understand Ka and Kha.’ They said, ‘What is Ka, even that is Kha; and what is Kha, even that is Ka’. Then the fires instructed him about Prana (Brahman) and the Akasa within the heart related to it.

sa: अथ हैनं गार्हपत्यो ऽनुशशास पृथिव्य् अग्निर् अन्नम् आदित्य इति ।
य एष आदित्ये पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहम् अस्मि स एव अहम् अस्मि इति ॥
iast: atha hainaṃ gārhapatyo ’nuśaśāsa pṛthivy agnir annam āditya iti ।
ya eṣa āditye puruṣo dṛśyate so ’ham asmi sa eva aham asmi iti ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: Then the Garhapatya fire instructed him: ‘Earth, fire, food and the sun (are my forms). The person who is seen in the sun, I am he, I am he, indeed.’

sa: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते ।
उप वयं तं भुञ्जामो ऽस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste ।
upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo ’smiṃś ca loke ’muṣmiṃś ca ।

tr.text: ‘He who knows it thus and meditates on it, destroys sinful acts, wins the region (of fire), reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, and his descendants never perish. We protect him in this world and in the next, who knows it thus and meditates on it.’

sa: अथ ह एनम् अन्वाहार्यपचनो ऽनुशशास आपो दिशो नक्षत्राणि चन्द्रमा इति ।
य एष चन्द्रमसि पुरुषो दृष्यते सो ऽहम् अस्मि स एव अहम् अस्मि इति ॥
iast: atha ha enam anvāhāryapacano ’nuśaśāsa āpo diśo nakṣatrāṇi candramā iti ।
ya eṣa candramasi puruṣo dṛṣyate so ’ham asmi sa eva aham asmi iti ॥
words: a star or any heavenly body

tr.text: Then the Anvaharyapacana fire instructed him: ‘Water, the quarters, the stars and the moon (are my forms). The person who is seen in the moon, I am he, I am he indeed.

sa: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते ।
उप वयं तं भुञ्जामो ऽस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste ।
upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo ’smiṃś ca loke ’muṣmiṃś ca ।

tr.text: ‘He who knows it thus and meditates on it, destroys sinful acts, wins the region (of fire), reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, and his descendants never perish. We protect him in this world and in the next, who knows it thus and meditates on it.’

sa: अथ हैनम् आहवनीयो ऽनुशशास प्राण आकाशो द्यौर् विद्युद् इति ।
य एष विद्युति पुरुषो दृश्यते सो ऽहम् अस्मि स एवाहम् अस्मीति ॥
iast: atha hainam āhavanīyo ’nuśaśāsa prāṇa ākāśo dyaur vidyud iti ।
ya eṣa vidyuti puruṣo dṛśyate so ’ham asmi sa evāham asmīti ॥
words: consecrated fire taken from the householder's perpetual fire and prepared for re
a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)
a flashing thunderbolt (as the weapon of the Maruts)

tr.text: Then the Ahavaniya fire instructed him, ‘Prana, Akasa, heaven and lightning (are my forms). The person who is seen in the lightning, I am he; I am he, indeed.

sa: स य एतम् एवं विद्वान् उपास्ते ।
उप वयं तं भुञ्जामो ऽस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च ।
iast: sa ya etam evaṃ vidvān upāste ।
upa vayaṃ taṃ bhuñjāmo ’smiṃś ca loke ’muṣmiṃś ca ।

tr.text: ‘He who knows it thus and meditates on it, destroys sinful acts, wins the region (of fire), reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, and his descendants never perish. We protect him in this world and in the next, who knows it thus and meditates on it.’

words: to address or salute with reverence

tr.text: The fires said, ‘O Upakosala, dear boy, to you (are revealed) this knowledge of the fires and the knowledge of the Atman; but the teacher will tell you the way.’ His teacher came back. The teacher addressed him ‘Upakosala !’

sa: को नु मानुशिश्याद् भो इतीहापेव निह्नुते ।
इमे नूनम् ईदृशा अन्यादृशा इतीहाग्नीन् अभ्यूदे ।
किं नु सोम्य किल ते ऽवोचन्न् इति ॥
iast: ko nu mānuśiśyād bho itīhāpeva nihnute ।
ime nūnam īdṛśā anyādṛśā itīhāgnīn abhyūde ।
kiṃ nu somya kila te ’vocann iti ॥
words: to address or salute with reverence
(a particle of asseveration or emphasis) indeed

tr.text: ‘Yes, revered sir’, he responded. ‘Dear boy, your face shines like that of a knower of Brahman ! who is it that has instructed you ?’ ‘Who should instruct me sir ?’, said he. Here he concealed the truth, as it were. ‘For this reason it is that though they were (formerly) otherwise they are now this wise’. So saying, he hinted at the (part played by the) fires in this matter. ‘What did they tell you, dear boy ?’

sa: लोकान् वाव किल सोम्य ते ऽवोचन् ।
अहं तु ते तद् वक्ष्यामि यथा पुष्करपलाश आपो न श्लिष्यन्त एवम् एवंविदि पापं कर्म न श्लिष्यत इति ।
iast: ahaṃ tu te tad vakṣyāmi yathā puṣkarapalāśa āpo na śliṣyanta evam evaṃvidi pāpaṃ karma na śliṣyata iti ।
words: (a particle of asseveration or emphasis) indeed

tr.text: ‘This’, thus he acknowledged. ‘Dear boy, they have told you about the regions only; but I shall tell you the object of your desire (i.e. Brahman). Just as water does not cling to the lotus-leaf, so also sin does not cling to him who knows Brahman thus’. ‘Revered sir, please instruct me further’. (The teacher) said to him:

sa: य एषो ऽक्षिणि पुरुषो दृश्यत एष आत्मेति होवाच ।
तद् यद्य् अप्य् अस्मिन् सर्पिर् वोदकं वा सिञ्चति वर्त्मनी एव गच्छति ॥
iast: ya eṣo ’kṣiṇi puruṣo dṛśyata eṣa ātmeti hovāca ।
tad yady apy asmin sarpir vodakaṃ vā siñcati vartmanī eva gacchati ॥
words: the track or rut of a wheel

tr.text: ‘This person who is seen in the eye, he is the Atman’, said the teacher; ‘this is the immortal, the fearless. This is Brahman. Hence, even if one sprinkles clarified butter or water into the eye, it goes away to the edges.’

sa: सर्वाण्य् एनं वामान्य् अभिसंयन्ति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: sarvāṇy enaṃ vāmāny abhisaṃyanti ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: ‘The knowers of Brahman call him as the centre of blessings; for all blessings come together in him. All blessings come together in him who knows thus.’

sa: सर्वाणि वामानि नयति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: sarvāṇi vāmāni nayati ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: ‘He, again, is the vehicle of blessings; for he carries all blessings. He who knows it thus carries all blessings. He who knows it thus carries all blessings.’

sa: सर्वेषु लोकेषु भाति य एवं वेद ॥
iast: sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda ॥

tr.text: ‘He again, is the vehicle of light; for he shines in all the regions. He who knows it thus shines in all the regions.’

sa: अथ यद् उ चैवास्मिञ् छव्यं कुर्वन्ति यदि च नार्चिषम् एवाभिसंभवन्ति ।
आपूर्यमाणपक्षाद् यान् षड् उदङ्ङ् एति मासांस् तान् ।
एतेन प्रतिपद्यमाना इमं मानवम् आवर्तं नावर्तन्ते नावर्तन्ते ॥
iast: atha yad u caivāsmiñ chavyaṃ kurvanti yadi ca nārciṣam evābhisaṃbhavanti ।
āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaḍ udaṅṅ eti māsāṃs tān ।
etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavam āvartaṃ nāvartante nāvartante ॥

tr.text: ‘Now, as for such persons, whether the cremation rites are performed or not, they go to light; from light to the day; from the day to the bright fortnight; from the bright fortnight to those six months during which (the sun) rises towards the north; from the months to the year; from the year to the sun; from the sun to the moon; from the moon to the lightning. (From the region of Brahman) a person, who is other than human, (comes and) causes them existing there, to realize Brahman. This is the path of the gods and the path to Brahman. Those who go by this path do not return to this human whirlpool – yes, they do not return.’

sa: एष ह वै यज्ञो यो ऽयं पवते ।
एष ह यन्न् इदं सर्वं पुनाति ।
यद् एष यन्न् इदं सर्वं पुनाति ।
तस्य मनश् च वाक् च वर्तनी ॥
iast: eṣa ha vai yajño yo ’yaṃ pavate ।
eṣa ha yann idaṃ sarvaṃ punāti ।

tr.text: He who blows (i.e. air) is indeed the sacrifice, he, moving along, purifies all this. And because moving along he purifies all this, he is the sacrifice. Mind and speech are the two paths of this sacrifice.

tr.text: One of these two paths, the Brahman priest embellishes with the mind. The Hotir, Adhvaryu and Udgatir priests embellish the other with speech. After the Prataranuvaka (the morning recitation) is commenced, and before the Paridhaniya Rik is begun, if the Brahman priest speaks out (breaking silence), then he embellishes only one path (viz. Speech) and the other is injured. Just as a man walking with one leg, or a chariot moving with one wheel suffers injury, so also that sacrifice of this one suffers injury, and when the sacrifice suffers injury, the sacrificer also suffers injury. For having completed the (defective) sacrifice, he becomes a worse sinner.

sa: स यथैकपाद् व्रजन् रथो वैकेन चक्रेण वर्तमानो रिष्यत्य् एवम् अस्य यज्ञो रिष्यति ।
iast: sa yathaikapād vrajan ratho vaikena cakreṇa vartamāno riṣyaty evam asya yajño riṣyati ।

tr.text: One of these two paths, the Brahman priest embellishes with the mind. The Hotir, Adhvaryu and Udgatir priests embellish the other with speech. After the Prataranuvaka (the morning recitation) is commenced, and before the Paridhaniya Rik is begun, if the Brahman priest speaks out (breaking silence), then he embellishes only one path (viz. Speech) and the other is injured. Just as a man walking with one leg, or a chariot moving with one wheel suffers injury, so also that sacrifice of this one suffers injury, and when the sacrifice suffers injury, the sacrificer also suffers injury. For having completed the (defective) sacrifice, he becomes a worse sinner.

sa: अथ यत्र उपाकृते प्रातरनुवाके न पुरा परिधानीयाया ब्रह्मा व्यववदत्य् उभे एव वर्तनी संस्कुर्वन्ति ।
iast: atha yatra upākṛte prātaranuvāke na purā paridhānīyāyā brahmā vyavavadaty ubhe eva vartanī saṃskurvanti ।

tr.text: But, after the Prataranuvaka is commenced and before the Paridhaniya Rik is begun, if the Brahman priest does not break his silence then both the paths are embellished; and neither one is injured.

sa: स यथोभयपाद् व्रजन् रथो वोभाभ्यां चक्राभ्यां वर्तमानः प्रतितिष्ठत्य् एवम् अस्य यज्ञः प्रतितिष्ठति यज्ञं प्रतितिष्ठन्तं यजमानो ऽनु प्रतितिष्ठति ।
iast: sa yathobhayapād vrajan ratho vobhābhyāṃ cakrābhyāṃ vartamānaḥ pratitiṣṭhaty evam asya yajñaḥ pratitiṣṭhati yajñaṃ pratitiṣṭhantaṃ yajamāno ’nu pratitiṣṭhati ।

tr.text: And just as a man walking with both the legs, or a chariot moving with both the wheels, remains intact, so also the sacrifice of this one remains intact. If the sacrifice remains intact, the sacrificer also remains intact. He becomes great by performing the sacrifice.

tr.text: Prajapati brooded on the worlds. From them thus brooded upon, he extracted their essences; fire from the earth, air from the sky and the sun from heaven.

tr.text: He brooded on these three deities. From them thus brooded upon, he extracted their essences: the Riks from fire, the Yajus-mantras from air, and the Saman from the sun.

tr.text: He brooded on the three Vedas. From them thus brooded upon, he extracted their existences; Bhuh from the Riks, Bhuvah from the Yajus-mantras and Svah from the Samans.

tr.text: Therefore if the sacrifice is rendered defective on account of the Riks, then with the Mantra ‘Bhuh Svaha’, (the Brahman priest) should offer an oblation in the Garhapatya fire. Thus verily, through the essence of the Riks, through the virility of the Riks, he makes good the injury of the sacrifice in respect of the Riks.

Thus verily, through the essence of the Yajus-mantras, through the virility of the Yajus-mantras, he makes good the injury of the sacrifice in respect of the Yajus-mantras.

tr.text: Just as one would join gold with salt, silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood with leather, even so does (the Brahman priest) make good the injury of the sacrifice through the virility of these regions, of these deities, and of the three Vedas. That sacrifice indeed is healed where there is a Brahman priest knowing thus.

sa: एवम् एषां लोकानाम् आसां देवतानाम् अस्यास् त्रय्या विद्याया वीर्येण यज्ञस्य विरिष्टं संदधाति ।
भेषजकृतो ह वा एष यज्ञो यत्रैवंविद् ब्रह्मा भवति ॥
iast: evam eṣāṃ lokānām āsāṃ devatānām asyās trayyā vidyāyā vīryeṇa yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdadhāti ।

tr.text: Just as one would join gold with salt, silver with gold, tin with silver, lead with tin, iron with lead, wood with iron, and wood with leather, even so does (the Brahman priest) make good the injury of the sacrifice through the virility of these regions, of these deities, and of the three Vedas. That sacrifice indeed is healed where there is a Brahman priest knowing thus.

एवंविदं ह वा एषा ब्रह्माणम् अनु गाथा ।
यतो यत आवर्तते तत् तद् गच्छति ॥

yato yata āvartate tat tad gacchati ॥

tr.text: That sacrifice indeed becomes inclined to the north, where there is a Brahman priest knowing thus. It is in reference to the Brahman priest knowing thus that there is this song: ‘Whence-soever the sacrifice comes back, thither verily does the Brahman priest go (to remedy)’.

sa: एवंविद् ध वै ब्रह्मा यज्ञं यजमानं सर्वांश् चर्त्विजो ऽभिरक्षति ।
तस्माद् एवंविदम् एव ब्रह्माणं कुर्वीत नानेवंविदं नानेवंविदम् ॥

tr.text: Just as the mare protects (the soldier), even so the silent Brahman priest is the only priest who protects the people engaged in rituals. The Brahman priest who knows thus verily protects the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and all the priests. Hence one should appoint as a Brahman priest only him who knows thus, not one who does not know thus – yea, not one who does not know thus.
